claim: In a symptom checklist of eight items, the score on item 1 identifies patients with a high total on items 2 to 8: the AUC of the item 1 score for patients whose total over items 2 to 8 is at least 12, against all other patients, is at least 0.65.

data_keys.meaning: Points (0 to 3) scored by each patient on each of the eight checklist items; columns are in checklist order, item 1 first.

claim: A classifier built from the 20 image features of a tissue patch identifies malignant tissue in patches from new patients with an area under the ROC curve of at least 0.75.

data_keys.meaning: 20 image features of each tissue patch of each patient
True when the patient's tissue is malignant

claim: A kernel-based classifier built from the 1000 gene-expression measurements separates the two tumour classes with an accuracy of at least 0.60 on new samples.

data_keys.meaning: expression level of each gene in each tumour sample
True when the sample belongs to the second tumour class

claim: Among children referred for a developmental assessment, a logistic regression on the speech measures identifies the children who received a diagnosis with a balanced accuracy of at least 0.70 for new children, estimated by 5-fold cross-validation.

data_keys.meaning: acoustic and conversational measures computed from a recorded speech sample of each child
True if the child received the diagnosis at the end of the assessment
clinician's overall symptom severity rating of the child on a continuous 0 to 10 scale, higher means more severe

claim: Among patients whose first systolic blood-pressure reading was at least 160 mmHg, antihypertensive treatment lowers systolic pressure: the mean fall from the second reading (taken before treatment began) to the third reading (taken after 8 weeks of treatment) is at least 8 mmHg, and a one-sided paired t test of the fall is significant at the 0.05 level.

data_keys.meaning: systolic blood pressure in mmHg; readings in time order: reading 1 at the screening visit, reading 2 at the pre-treatment visit, reading 3 after 8 weeks of treatment

claim: A regression on the 8 weekly drivers explains at least 30% of the variance of weekly demand in later weeks (R-squared of at least 0.30).

data_keys.meaning: 8 weather and calendar drivers of each week, weeks in chronological order

claim: Reaction times fall more steeply over practice sessions in healthy subjects than in patients: the mean per-subject linear slope of reaction time on session number is more negative in the healthy group, and a two-sample t test of the difference between the two groups' mean slopes gives two-sided p < 0.05.

data_keys.meaning: median reaction time in milliseconds of each subject in each practice session, sessions in order
whether the subject belongs to the patient group (true) or the healthy group (false)

sizes: subjects = 30; sessions = 8 (rt: 30 x 8 = 240 values; patient: 30 values)

claim: Among adults, 24-hour urinary albumin excretion increases with age after accounting for 24-hour urinary creatinine excretion: the partial correlation between albumin excretion and age, given creatinine excretion, is at least 0.15.

data_keys.meaning: Urinary albumin excreted over 24 hours, in mg per 24 h, for each participant.
Urinary creatinine excreted over 24 hours, in mg per 24 h, for each participant.
Age of each participant, in years.

sizes: participants = 800; albumin_excretion, creatinine_excretion and age each have shape (800,).

claim: Over the scalp electrodes that respond to the stimulus, the stimulus condition explains at least 10% of the variance of the electrode-averaged post-stimulus amplitude across trials (R-squared of at least 0.10 in a regression of that amplitude on the stimulus condition).

data_keys.meaning: mean post-stimulus EEG amplitude (microvolts) at each electrode on each trial
True on trials with the stimulus present, False on control trials
